newsitem.title: USA: NYSE Jan 6-10 program trading averages 12.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE Jan 6-10 program trading averages 12.3 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading averaged 12.3 percent of its average daily volume of 544.2 million shares, or 67.0 million shares, for the week of January 6-10.
Program trading accounted for an average of 15.4 percent of average daily volume of 413.3 million shares for the week of December 30, 1996 to January 3, 1997.
Of the average 67.0 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 32.6 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 34.4 million daily.
In all markets, program trading averaged 92.8 million shares a day during the week of January 6-10.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, BNP Securities and Salomon Brothers executed most or all of their program activity for customers, as agent or facilitator. Morgan Stanley, Lehman Brothers and Nomura Securities executed most of their program activity as principal, for their own accounts.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 65.4 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 34.1 percent of program volume from January 6-10.

Between January 6 and 10, 29.0 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 0.8 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
